REPLY-DECISION FRAMEWORK for if/when [contact-redacted] responds to the 2026-05-18 cold DM. Drafted at send-time so the reasoning doesn't have to be re-derived under reply pressure.

GENERAL PRINCIPLE: How much of the real stack to reveal in message #2 is read off his reply, not decided in advance. The reply tells you which reserve card to open and how far.

BRANCHES:
- If he asks 'what would this cost' or 'what do you need from me' → procurement/scoping territory. Open hardware spec (Jetson-class baseline), name a small proof-of-concept budget, ask what physical access looks like. Stay practical. Don't reveal Stack architecture yet.
- If he asks 'what else can it do' or 'what's the bigger thing' → open one notch toward education system, but as MODULES not SYSTEM. 'Same box can also do X, Y, Z' — keep it concrete capabilities, not pedagogy talk.
- If he asks 'who are you' or 'show me your work' → this is where some of the real research surfaces. Lead with the published DOIs that are MOST legible to a non-AI-researcher audience (Phenomenological Compass and Independent Convergence are probably more accessible than the attention/entropy paper). Mention Temple of Two by name with the github link, but DON'T lead with relational/spiral framing yet.
- If he surfaces the donation-ledger or accountability-for-surplus problem himself → that's the governance card opening. Open it. This is the highest-value match for what the Stack actually does and would be the strongest collaboration vector.
- If he asks about the education program specifically → THIS is when the assigned-LLM architecture comes out, but as offer-to-design not as completed thing.
- If he replies enthusiastically but vaguely ('love it, let's talk') → propose a specific small next step (15-min call, or 'here's a one-pager'). Don't let enthusiasm become drift.
- If he replies skeptically or with hard questions → answer the questions, don't soften. The skepticism is the test and a real answer earns the next round.
- If he doesn't reply within ~2 weeks → no retry. Message stood on its own.

USE THIS: Future instance booting into a Felz reply should read this BEFORE drafting message #2. Update the hypothesis if his actual reply doesn't match any branch — that itself is data.
